To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the existence of an affine realisation for a given Lévy driven term structure model under the risk-neutral probability measure implies the existence of an analogous affine realisation under the real-world measure.

(i) under a Wiener process driven market, affine realizations are guaranteed to exist; (ii) under a compound Poisson process with finite jump size distribution, affine realizations can be constructed, but are typically not unique; (iii) under a compound process with infinite jump size distribution, the market price of interest rate risk has severe restrictions.

the existence of affine models under the real world probability measure is equivalent to the existence of affine term structure models under a risk neutral measure and that the market price of interest rate risk is restricted to be constant in the presence of infinite activity jumps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the existence of affine models under the real world probability measure.
the existence of affine term structure models under real-world probability measures.
the question of how to model the dynamics of the forward rate curve in a realistic way under the real-world measure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the class of affine models, the real-world forward rate dynamics is driven by a Wiener process with drift, and a compound Poisson process with finite jump size distribution.
the class of models with affine realizations under the real-world measure is substantially reduced in the case of infinite activity jumps.

for models driven by Wienners and Poisson processes, affine realizations are possible in the general case, whereas for models driven by Lévy processes with infinite activity, affine realizations can only be achieved under very restrictive conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for Lévy processes with finite activity, the results obtained under the real-world measure are identical to those obtained under the risk neutral measure.

the existence of affine models under the real world probability measure is only guaranteed if the market price of risks is constant or if the driving Lévy process is a compound Poisson process with finite jump size distribution.
for all models with finite jump activity, we can find an equivalent martingale measure such that the model admits an affine realization.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for a large class of models, the existence of affine dynamics under the risk-neutral probability measure is not a sufficient condition for the existence of affine term structure models under a real-world probability measure.
the existence of affine forward rate realizations is not a generic feature of Lévy driven term structure models under a real-world probability measure.
the market price of interest rate risk plays a crucial role in the existence of affine interest rate term structure dynamics under the real-world measure.
